claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let's look into whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, his continued eligibility for Child Benefit depends on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? If so, could you tell me a bit more about what he's studying or the type of course he's on?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment. He finished school but he's not doing any courses or training right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course, there are a couple more things I need to check.

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), or has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for training or work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with anyone yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more question about Alex's situation.

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week in a paid job?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question to help determine eligibility.

When did Alex leave school? Specifically, was it after the last official school leaving date (which is typically the last Friday in June for those finishing compulsory education)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he left after the summer - after that last Friday in June.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He left school after the official school leaving date (last Friday in June)
- He is not currently in full-time education or on an approved training course
- He has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation
- He is not working 24 hours or more per week

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 16):**
Child Benefit can continue for a 16-year-old after leaving school only if they:
1. Continue in approved full-time education or training, OR
2. Register with a careers service (such as Connexions) while awaiting a place in education or training

Since Alex has left school after the official school leaving date, is not currently in education or training, and hasn't registered with a careers service, he doesn't meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit.

**What you could do:**
If Alex were to:
- Start an approved full-time education course (such as A-levels or a college course), or
- Begin an approved training course, or
- Register with a careers service while looking for education or training opportunities

...then you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him again until he turns 20 (as long as he remains in qualifying education or training).

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and has left school after the official school leaving date (last Friday in June). Child Benefit can continue for 16-year-olds who have left education only if they: (1) are in approved full-time education or training, OR (2) have registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation and are awaiting a place on approved education/training, or are not working 24+ hours per week. Since Alex is not in education or training, and has not registered with any careers service or similar organisation, he does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit eligibility. The extension period that applies after leaving education only covers the period until the official school leaving date or a short period after if registered appropriately, which does not apply in Alex's case.
